description: Mirror the SETLISTS store into app.db (Setlists table, same mirror pattern as FEAT-001), wire the shared app.db path through the MainWindow construction site, update the existing song tests to inject a temp app.db with ClearAllPools teardown, and add the new one-time-import + FolderPath-contract tests. Setlist JSON files stay authoritative on disk; ServiceOrderManager.CreateFromSetlist is unaffected (it consumes an in-memory Setlist). Depends on FEAT-001 (reuses the AppDatabase field, _initialized guard, EnsureInitializedAsync, and SongPathResolver.Normalize key helper added there).
steps: Read FIRST (absolute worktree paths): .agents/tasks/sql-phase06/context.json and this file; then re-read SongManager.cs as modified by FEAT-001, WorshipPlayer.Core/Models/Setlist.cs, WorshipPlayer.UI/Views/MainWindow.xaml.cs (around line 131), WorshipPlayer.UI/Services/PresenterIntegration.cs (lines 85-115), and the three test files to modify plus SongLibraryServiceTests.Dispose for the ClearAllPools pattern.

In SongManager.cs add the Setlists DDL const: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Setlists (FilePath TEXT PRIMARY KEY, Name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', Date TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', LastWriteUtc TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', DataJson TEXT NOT NULL); run it inside EnsureInitializedAsync alongside the Songs DDL (both CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, order irrelevant).

Add a BindSetlist(cmd, Setlist, normalizedFilePath) + UpsertSetlistRowAsync(connection, transaction, setlist, filePath) using ON CONFLICT(FilePath) DO UPDATE SET (DataJson = JsonSerializer.Serialize(setlist, _jsonOptions); promoted Name/Date from the Setlist; LastWriteUtc from the file when it exists else UtcNow). Key = SongPathResolver.Normalize(filePath).

In SaveSetlistAsync: after 'await File.WriteAllTextAsync(filePath, json);' add a best-effort UpsertSetlistRowSafeAsync(setlist, filePath) (try/catch-swallow). The setlist file is authoritative and written first.

In LoadAllSetlistsAsync: track each scanned (filePath, setlist) pair, and after the scan add a best-effort ReconcileSetlistsSafeAsync that upserts each scanned setlist and prunes Setlists rows whose FilePath is NOT IN the scanned set (same NOT IN shape as the Songs reconcile). Do not change the scan or the returned in-memory list.

Extend the one-time import: in EnsureInitializedAsync's import step, add ImportSetlistsIfNeededAsync(connection) that, when the Setlists table is empty and _setlistsBasePath exists, imports each <SetlistsFolder>/*.json as a mirror row (INSERT OR IGNORE, tolerate missing/malformed, never throw). Leave the setlist JSON files on disk.

Wire construction: in WorshipPlayer.UI/Views/MainWindow.xaml.cs at the 'new SongManager(songsPath, setlistsPath)' call (~line 131), compute the app.db path as Path.Combine(AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory, "app.db") (matching PresenterIntegration.cs:85-86) and pass it as the 3rd arg. Add a one-line comment mirroring the Phase-5 wording: JSON song/setlist files stay authoritative; app.db is a reconciled mirror. Verify PresenterIntegration.cs needs no change (SongLibraryService still just wraps the SongManager).

Update existing tests to inject a temp app.db (3rd SongManager arg) and clear pools in teardown, preserving every current assertion: SongLibraryServiceTests.cs (ctor at ~line 32 already has dbPath — pass it to new SongManager; also pass a temp app.db to the two reload managers at ~255 and ~338; its Dispose already calls ClearAllPools). SongPathResolverTests.cs SongManagerDedupTests (add a temp app.db path field, pass as 3rd arg at ~line 146, add SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools() at the start of Dispose). ChordProImportTests.cs (add a temp app.db path, pass as 3rd SongManager arg at ~line 36, add SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools() in Dispose before Directory.Delete). Add 'using Microsoft.Data.Sqlite;' where needed.

Add new test file WorshipPlayer.Tests/SongManagerSqliteMirrorTests.cs (xUnit, IDisposable, temp root under Path.GetTempPath(), SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools() in Dispose): (1) ImportsOnDiskSongsAndSetlists_IntoMirror_NonDuplicating — write two song folders with song.json (metadata + a section + a track) and one setlist .json; construct SongManager(songs, setlists, tempAppDb); await LoadAllSongsAsync + LoadAllSetlistsAsync; open the temp app.db and assert SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Songs == 2 and FROM Setlists == 1, and that a Song DataJson round-trips with its section/track intact; then construct a SECOND SongManager on the same folders+db, load again, and assert the counts are unchanged (non-duplicating). (2) MirrorKey_IsNormalizedFolderPath_UpsertNotDuplicate — save a song, then save it again after setting FolderPath to a case/separator variant of the same path, and assert SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Songs == 1 and the single row's FolderPath equals SongPathResolver.Normalize(folder) (FolderPath identity contract).
Run the FULL test suite and the full build (final cross-cutting verification) and record the exact pass counts in findings.
acceptance_criteria: After SaveSetlistAsync, app.db Setlists has one row keyed by the normalized setlist file path whose DataJson round-trips to the saved Setlist; the setlist .json file is still written first and authoritative.
ServiceOrderManager.CreateFromSetlist behavior is unchanged (no edits to ServiceOrderManager).
MainWindow constructs SongManager with the shared app.db path as the 3rd arg; the build is clean (0 errors, 4 pre-existing warnings).

SongLibraryServiceTests, SongPathResolverTests (incl. SongManagerDedupTests), and ChordProImportTests inject a temp app.db and call SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools() in teardown; all their existing assertions still pass.

The new SongManagerSqliteMirrorTests pass: one-time import is non-duplicating on a second load, and the mirror key equals SongPathResolver.Normalize(FolderPath) with a case/separator variant upserting the SAME row.
The full test suite is green (>= 607 baseline + the new tests).
verification: Run: dotnet build "c:\Users\Quang\Documents\OneWorshipcenter\owc-multitrack-feature-lyric-presenter\owc-multitrack-feature-lyric-presenter\.worktrees\sql-phase06\WorshipBacktrackPlayer.sln" -c Debug  — expect 0 errors, 4 warnings.

Run: dotnet test "c:\Users\Quang\Documents\OneWorshipcenter\owc-multitrack-feature-lyric-presenter\owc-multitrack-feature-lyric-presenter\.worktrees\sql-phase06\WorshipPlayer.Tests\WorshipPlayer.Tests.csproj"  — ALL tests pass (baseline 607 plus the new mirror tests; zero regressions).
findings: Implemented in SongManager.cs (Setlists mirror), MainWindow.xaml.cs (wiring), the three existing song test files (temp app.db + ClearAllPools), and the new SongManagerSqliteMirrorTests.cs. SongManager now: (a) adds CreateSetlistsSchemaSql const (FilePath PK + Name/Date/LastWriteUtc + DataJson), run in EnsureInitializedAsync alongside the Songs DDL, plus ImportSetlistsIfNeededAsync; (b) SaveSetlistAsync calls UpsertSetlistRowSafeAsync strictly AFTER the authoritative setlist .json write; (c) LoadAllSetlistsAsync tracks scanned (path,setlist) pairs and calls ReconcileSetlistsSafeAsync (upsert present, parameterized NOT IN prune, DELETE all when empty) AFTER the scan, leaving the returned in-memory Setlists list/order unchanged; (d) added UpsertSetlistRowAsync (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(FilePath) DO UPDATE), BindSetlist (key = SongPathResolver.Normalize(filePath); LastWriteUtc from file else UtcNow ISO-8601 'o'; DataJson via _jsonOptions), all best-effort try/catch-swallow. ServiceOrderManager untouched; setlist JSON stays authoritative. Wiring: MainWindow.xaml.cs passes the existing appDbPath (Path.Combine(BaseDirectory,'app.db') computed at line 56) as the 3rd SongManager arg with a Phase-6 comment; PresenterIntegration.cs needed no change. Tests: SongLibraryServiceTests injects _appDbPath into the ctor manager + both reload managers (Dispose already clears pools); SongPathResolverTests.SongManagerDedupTests gains a temp app.db field, passes it as 3rd arg, adds SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools() + 'using Microsoft.Data.Sqlite;'; ChordProImportTests gains a temp app.db field, passes it, adds ClearAllPools in Dispose + the using. New SongManagerSqliteMirrorTests: (1) ImportsOnDiskSongsAndSetlists_IntoMirror_NonDuplicating asserts Songs==2/Setlists==1, DataJson round-trips section+track, and a second manager on the same folders+db leaves counts unchanged; (2) MirrorKey_IsNormalizedFolderPath_UpsertNotDuplicate asserts a case/separator variant upserts the SAME row (Songs==1) and the stored FolderPath equals SongPathResolver.Normalize(folder). FINDING: Path.GetFullPath does NOT canonicalize Windows casing, so Normalize('C:\x') and Normalize('C:\X\') differ by case and the default case-SENSITIVE SQLite PK produced 2 rows, violating the FolderPath identity contract the acceptance criterion requires (and the app-wide SongPathResolver OrdinalIgnoreCase identity). Behavior-preserving fix applied to the mirror schema only: FolderPath/FilePath PKs declared TEXT PRIMARY KEY COLLATE NOCASE so the internal reconciled mirror honors the same case-insensitive identity. No user-visible or system-behavior change (authoritative JSON files and in-memory lists untouched). Verification: clean rebuild = 0 errors / 4 pre-existing warnings; full suite = 609 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (607 baseline + 2 new mirror tests, zero regressions).
